title: Brokers and broker contacts backend
objective: Tenant broker administration: list, add, edit, disable brokers with typed tier, branch, and contacts (one primary), per spec FR-24 and PRD 12.10.
scope: CRUD + disable endpoints and contact management
Active-broker picker query for intake and settings
implementation_details: Liquibase 070-brokers: brokers (tenant_id, id identity, name text not null, broker_type_id bigint null FK reference_items, branch text null, status text check in ('active','disabled'), audit cols, PK (tenant_id,id), unique (tenant_id, name)); broker_contacts (tenant_id, id identity, broker_id bigint, name, email, phone, is_primary bool, PK (tenant_id,id))

Features/Brokers: CreateBrokerCommand (name required; broker_type must be active BrokerType reference item), UpdateBrokerCommand, DisableBrokerCommand (disabled brokers hidden from pickers, retained on historical records), GetBrokerQuery (incl. contacts), ListBrokersQuery (filter status/type/search, paged); contact subcommands AddContact/UpdateContact/RemoveContact/SetPrimaryContact with invariant exactly-one-primary when any contact exists (enforced in handler transaction)

Endpoints: GET/POST /api/v1/brokers, GET/PUT /api/v1/brokers/{id}, POST /api/v1/brokers/{id}/disable, POST/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/brokers/{id}/contacts[/{contactId}], POST .../contacts/{contactId}/set-primary — RequirePermission(Brokers.Manage) for writes, Brokers.View for reads

findings.description: RemoveContactCommandHandler is non-atomic when removing the primary contact. RemoveContactAsync commits its own SaveChanges, then the promotion of the new primary is a SECOND SaveChanges. Between the two commits there is a transient zero-primary window, and if the second commit fails (DB error/cancellation) the broker is persisted with contacts but NO primary — violating the exactly-one-primary invariant the task explicitly required to be partial-update-safe. Add and SetPrimary are already atomic (single SaveChanges); only RemoveContact has this gap.
findings.recommendation: Promote remaining[0] in-memory BEFORE removing the target and let a single SaveChanges cover both the delete and the demote/promote, so removal + re-establishment of the invariant commit atomically.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit). RemoveContactCommandHandler.cs:58-61 computes the promotion candidate (oldest remaining by lowest id) up front and makes a single store call; BrokerStore.RemoveContactAsync (BrokerStore.cs:151-165) wraps delete + promote in one explicit BeginTransactionAsync/CommitAsync (delete flushed before promote), so either both persist or neither rolls back together and the DB never holds two primaries mid-transaction. Non-primary removal leaves primary unchanged; last-contact removal sets promote=null (no spurious promotion). New test RemoveContact_WhenRemovingPrimary_ShouldCommitDeletionAndPromotionAtomically queries broker_contacts directly (not via API) proving the single committed state; the two prior RemoveContact tests retain full assertions unweakened.

findings.description: The one-primary invariant is enforced purely in application handlers with no DB-level guard (no partial unique index on broker_contacts (tenant_id, broker_id) WHERE is_primary, no row lock/serialized transaction). Two concurrent AddContact(isPrimary=true) or SetPrimary requests against the same broker can interleave read-then-write and leave two primaries. Consistent with the accepted BusinessAssignment.IsAccountableOwner precedent, so recorded for parity/hardening rather than as novel.
findings.recommendation: Add a partitioned partial unique index enforcing at most one primary per broker per tenant (Liquibase changeset), which also converts F-042's transient double-primary into a hard DB error. Optional hardening.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit incl. partition-propagation proof). Appended Liquibase changeset 072-broker-contacts-primary-unique-index (070-brokers.xml:97-104, prior changesets untouched) creates uq_broker_contacts_primary ON broker_contacts (tenant_id, broker_id) WHERE is_primary=true. Because tenant_id (LIST partition key) is an indexed column, Postgres allows the unique index on the partitioned parent and auto-propagates it to all existing AND future partitions; evaluator independently reproduced this (built a partitioned parent, created a future partition via the exact production CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF DDL that create_tenant_partitions.sql:24-29 uses, confirmed the inherited partial unique index rejected a second primary with 23505). Migrations run before any runtime tenant creation, so every production per-tenant partition inherits the guard. Add/SetPrimary hardened (AddContactAsync/SetPrimaryAsync flush the demote before insert/promote in one transaction) so legitimate happy paths never transiently violate the index; no happy path regressed. New tests assert SqlState 23505 on a raw second-primary insert bypassing the handlers, and index inheritance on a tenant partition. Applied live + idempotent (Run 1 then Run 0).

findings.description: Dead permission surface: PermissionCatalog.Brokers still declares and registers six granular codes (Create, Update, Disable, ManageContacts, ManageApiAccess, ViewPerformance) that no endpoint references. Gating on coarse Brokers.View/Manage is correct per the task brief, but the unused codes are confusing catalog surface.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused granular broker codes, OR add a comment marking them reserved for T-030 (broker API access) / T-034 (broker performance) so it is unambiguous which codes actually gate access. Note ManageApiAccess/ViewPerformance may legitimately be reserved for those later tasks — keep those with a reserved-comment and remove only the truly-superseded ones (Create/Update/Disable/ManageContacts).
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit). Brokers.Create/Update/Disable/ManageContacts removed from both the constants and the All list (PermissionCatalog.cs:122-132, 254-257); Brokers now exposes only View, Manage, ManageApiAccess, ViewPerformance. ManageApiAccess/ViewPerformance retained with explicit reserved-for-T-030 / reserved-for-T-034 comments. Grep across the whole src tree found no reference to the removed codes anywhere (endpoints, seeders, RBAC wiring, tests). PermissionCatalogSeederTests iterates PermissionCatalog.All dynamically with no hardcoded count, so nothing silently broke; removed codes were never granted in seed data so nothing was orphaned.

history.message: Task generated from approved spec.md (FR-24, PRD 12.10)

T-012 IN_PROGRESS; delegated to Implementor (iteration 1/10). Dep T-008 PASS. Test-first (integration real Postgres + Keycloak Testcontainers, no mocks, AAA): Liquibase 070-brokers brokers + broker_contacts tables (partitioned), CRUD + disable + contact management with exactly-one-primary invariant, active-broker picker (disabled hidden but retained on records), broker_type must be active BrokerType reference item, Brokers.Manage writes / Brokers.View reads, all mutations audited.

Evaluation (iteration 1/10): VERDICT PASS on all five gates (evaluator recommended PASS). Independent suite (clean single run, no flakes): Domain 9/9, Infrastructure 45/45, Api 163/163 = 217/217. Completeness AC-023/V-023/FR-24 satisfied: list/create/edit/disable + contacts; IsActiveBrokerTypeAsync genuinely validates list_type==BrokerType AND IsActive AND tenant scope; disable is soft + hidden from active picker but retained; audit before/after present+tested. Exactly-one-primary: Add + SetPrimary atomic (single SaveChanges) and correct; auto-promote-lowest-id on primary removal is an acceptable documented assumption. Schema/partitioning correct (composite PK, identity, LIST partition + default, registered in create_tenant_partitions + master, no EF/JSONB); no-physical-FK consistent with existing convention + app-level integrity enforced. Tenant isolation: by-id cross-tenant returns 404 (no oracle, matches T-007 F-027/spec 14); the separate 403 test is a pre-handler membership gate on a spoofed X-Tenant-Id revealing nothing — both correct. 13 real integration tests, non-tautological, none weakened. Playwright V-023 brokers test.fixme legitimate (Settings UI T-016). NON-BLOCKING findings: F-042 (minor correctness: RemoveContact primary-removal non-atomic, two SaveChanges -> transient zero-primary + persisted-zero-primary-on-second-commit-failure, violates the partial-update-safety the task required), F-043 (minor concurrency: one-primary enforced app-only, no DB partial-unique-index; consistent with accepted IsAccountableOwner precedent), F-044 (minor maintainability: dead granular broker permission codes). Orchestrator decision: route back for a focused fix iteration to close F-042 (real defect on an explicit requirement) + F-043 hardening + F-044 cleanup rather than defer.

T-012 NEEDS_FIXES; fix iteration 2/10 delegated to Implementor for F-042 (make RemoveContact primary-removal atomic: promote remaining[0] in-memory before delete, single SaveChanges), F-043 (add a partitioned partial unique index enforcing at most one primary per broker per tenant via Liquibase, DB-level hardening that also makes any double-primary a hard error), F-044 (remove superseded granular broker codes Create/Update/Disable/ManageContacts; keep ManageApiAccess/ViewPerformance with a reserved-for-T-030/T-034 comment). iteration_count -> 2.

T-012 fix iteration 2/10 IMPLEMENTED. F-042 fixed: IBrokerStore.RemoveContactAsync(contact, promote?, ct) now does delete-then-promote in ONE explicit DB transaction (Begin -> delete+SaveChanges -> promote+SaveChanges -> Commit); handler computes the promotion candidate up front and makes a single call; the prior second independent SaveChanges is gone; deleting old primary before promoting avoids ever having two is_primary rows. F-043 fixed: new appended Liquibase changeset 072-broker-contacts-primary-unique-index creates UNIQUE INDEX uq_broker_contacts_primary ON broker_contacts (tenant_id, broker_id) WHERE is_primary=true; since tenant_id (LIST partition key) is an indexed column Postgres allows the unique index directly on the partitioned parent and auto-attaches it to all existing + future partitions (verified), so no create_tenant_partitions change needed; applied live (Run 1, then Run 0 idempotent), \d broker_contacts confirms the partial unique index. Add/SetPrimary handlers hardened: demote flushed via SaveChanges BEFORE insert/promote, both wrapped in one transaction via new IBrokerStore.AddContactAsync(contact, demote, ct) / SetPrimaryAsync(target, demote, ct), so the index is never transiently violated and ops stay all-or-nothing. F-044 fixed: removed Brokers.Create/Update/Disable/ManageContacts (constants + All entries; covered by Brokers.Manage); kept Brokers.ManageApiAccess/ViewPerformance each with a reserved-for-T-030/T-034 summary comment; PermissionCatalogSeederTests iterates PermissionCatalog.All dynamically so no count test needed adjusting; grep confirmed no other references to the removed codes. 3 new integration tests (real Postgres+Keycloak, no mocks): RemoveContact_WhenRemovingPrimary_ShouldCommitDeletionAndPromotionAtomically (queries broker_contacts directly), BrokerContacts_WhenSecondPrimaryInsertedDirectly_ShouldBeRejectedByDatabaseUniqueIndex (raw SQL insert asserts SqlState 23505), BrokerContactsPrimaryUniqueIndex_ShouldApplyToTenantSpecificPartition (materializes broker_contacts_p{tenantId} and proves the inherited index rejects a second primary on a tenant partition). Existing RemoveContact promote/non-primary tests remain green, unweakened. Full backend suite twice: Domain 9/9, Infrastructure 45/45, Api 166/166 = 220/220, no flakes; build 0 warnings/0 errors; Liquibase live-applied + idempotent. Harness JSON untouched.
